name: Cascade
description: Replays little loops of what you just played, stacked at octave (and fifth) speeds in a pattern you can hear, so one note comes back as a shimmering, rhythmic cascade of itself.

params.name: Pattern
params.description: How each captured slice is replayed. Mosaic loops it at several speeds at once. Strum strikes the start of it again and again in a run that quickens or slows. Tunnel loops a short piece of it into a steady drone that grows longer and darker. Steps plays each repeat at the next speed, like an arpeggio of the note.

params.name: Time
params.description: How long after a note it first comes back, and the pulse its repeats fall on. Short times give a fast glittering stutter; long times replay whole phrases.

params.name: Repeats
params.description: How many times each slice comes back before it stops, which sets how long the cascade goes on after you stop playing.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How much quieter and darker each repeat is than the one before. At zero every repeat is as loud and as bright as the first.

params.name: High
params.description: Level of the replays that run faster than you played. They sound an octave or more above and come round two or four times in the space of one slower repeat.

params.name: Low
params.description: Level of a half-speed replay: the slice an octave down and twice as long, underneath the rest and in the middle of the stereo picture.

params.name: Interval
params.description: Which speeds the faster replays use. Octaves keeps everything on the note you played. Octaves and fifths adds replays a fifth above, which also fall three against two with the rest.

params.name: Shape
params.description: The envelope of every replay. Low gives sharp plucked fronts that die away; high makes each one swell in and out, so the pattern blurs into a wash.

params.name: Reverse
params.description: The chance that a replay runs backwards. Zero is all forwards; full is all backwards.

params.name: Spread
params.description: How far the replays are placed to the left and right. The faster ones sit furthest out and swap sides as they repeat.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Takes the highs off all the replays. Lower settings make the cascade softer and further away.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the cascade.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. In the family of micro-looping pedals: the input is cut into slices on a clock (restarted at note onsets) and each slice is replayed by a pool of windowed loop voices at speeds of 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 3 and 4, the time-domain transposition of windowed fragments described in Curtis Roads, 'Microsound' (2001). Faster voices read half-band decimated copies of the buffer so they do not alias (the mip-map of Lance Williams, 'Pyramidal Parametrics', 1983, applied to audio). The Tunnel drone cuts its loop to a whole number of cycles found with the difference function of A. de Cheveigne and H. Kawahara, 'YIN, a fundamental frequency estimator for speech and music' (2002). Not a model of any unit.
